inputs.text: Cuba is apparently heading into a political shakeup, but the usual progressive outcry over deepening inequalities and ordinary people being shut out is just the same tired rhetoric. The real problem is how decades of failed collectivist policies have left families without the resources or habits of personal responsibility needed to build anything lasting. Allowing the wealthy diaspora and foreign investors to step in and acquire assets is not some plot to entrench elite power—it's the natural outcome of opening up a stagnant system, and it could bring the capital and enterprise that actually creates work and opportunity. Calls to center everything on labor rights and shield the disadvantaged sound noble but usually just prolong dependency and block the cultural continuity that comes from strong families, national self-reliance, and traditional authority. What Cuba needs is less of this structural exploitation narrative and more room for free initiative to restore order and prosperity.
